pat.certification-bottlenecks.fix: Set up certification capacity before the duty applies, limit certifier conflicts and allow alternatives.
pat.certification-bottlenecks.ex_ai: AI bills can tie compliance to certified audits or accredited evaluators that may not exist yet, or that are paid by the developers they assess.
pat.future-amendments-incorporated.plain: Referencing standards as amended from time to time changes the law's content without a new vote, handing control to whoever maintains the document.
pat.future-amendments-incorporated.check: Find each reference to a standard or document 'as amended'. Ask who can change that document, whether the legislature reviews changes, and whether the version is fixed by date.
pat.future-amendments-incorporated.fix: Fix the referenced version by date and require review before adopting changes.
pat.advisory-capture.plain: Seats set aside for industry or members chosen for industry experience can give regulated parties a leading role in drafting the rules.
pat.advisory-capture.check: Read who sits on each advisory body and who picks them. Ask whether seats are reserved for the parties being regulated, whether public interest seats exist, and whether recommendations must be published or can bind the agency.
pat.advisory-capture.fix: Set balanced membership with public interest seats, conflict rules and published recommendations.
pat.advisory-capture.ex_ai: AI bills can reserve advisory seats for developers or members chosen for technical expertise, which can give them the leading role in drafting the rules.
pat.record-flooding.plain: Record requirements and duties to respond to comments reward large volumes of submissions, which can be used to build a litigation record or overwhelm review.
pat.record-flooding.check: Read the record and comment duties placed on decision makers. Ask whether duplicate or bulk submissions must each be answered, and whether the agency may group them.
pat.record-flooding.fix: Allow the agency to group duplicate comments and limit response duty to distinct issues.
pat.record-flooding.ex_ai: AI bills can reward large volumes of submissions that build a litigation record or overwhelm agency review.
pat.stakeholder-process.plain: Consensus requirements in stakeholder processes can give a veto to the best organized participants, and expertise weighting or short timelines can sideline others.
pat.stakeholder-process.check: Find any advisory or standard-setting group. Ask who sits on it, how it decides, whether consensus gives a veto, how long it has, and whether the agency may depart from its output.
pat.stakeholder-process.fix: Set balanced membership, majority or reasoned decisions, adequate time and agency authority to decide.
pat.stakeholder-process.ex_ai: Consensus requirements in stakeholder processes give a veto to industry, and expertise weighting or short timelines can marginalize civil society.
pat.stakeholder-process.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on telecom standards could require consensus of a working group, so any single large member can block a rule.
pat.comment-period-timing.plain: Short comment windows for complex rules, especially across holidays, limit how much the public and experts can take part.
pat.comment-period-timing.check: Find comment, notice or hearing periods. Ask how long they run relative to the complexity of the proposal, whether they span holidays, and whether extensions are available.
pat.comment-period-timing.fix: Set comment periods in proportion to complexity and allow extension on request.
pat.comment-period-timing.ex_ai: Short comment windows for complex rules, including over holidays, limit public participation.
pat.comment-period-timing.ex_other: For illustration: A land use rule of several hundred pages might open for comment for thirty days over a holiday period.
pat.technical-capacity-limits.plain: Barring internal testing tools, requiring reliance on outside assessors, or setting low pay scales can reduce a regulator's own ability to evaluate.
pat.technical-capacity-limits.check: Find limits on the regulator's staffing, tools, pay and contracting. Ask whether it can test or investigate by itself, or must rely on the regulated party or paid third parties.
pat.technical-capacity-limits.fix: Authorize the regulator to build its own testing capacity and set competitive pay.
pat.technical-capacity-limits.ex_ai: Barring internal testing tools, requiring third-party assessments or low pay scales reduces the regulator's own ability to evaluate.
pat.technical-capacity-limits.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on building inspections could require agencies to accept private inspector reports and bar them from buying testing equipment.
pat.study-instead-of-action.plain: Requiring a study or report in place of a concrete outcome gives the appearance of progress while action is deferred.
pat.study-instead-of-action.check: Find each study, report or assessment. Ask what action follows it, by when, and whether the outcome changes anything if the report is late or never written.
pat.study-instead-of-action.fix: Attach an action or default rule to each report and set deadlines.
pat.study-it-to-death.plain: Chained assessments each with its own timeline, comment period and challenge mean implementation is always one study away.
pat.study-it-to-death.check: Trace chains of studies where one report leads to another. Ask whether the text sets an end point, and what happens automatically when the last report is delivered.
pat.study-it-to-death.fix: Limit to one study with a deadline and an automatic next step.
pat.transparency-defined-down.plain: A bare notice that something exists or applies is less informative than disclosing how it works and its limits, and a law can require only the former.
pat.transparency-defined-down.check: Find what exactly must be disclosed and to whom. Ask whether the disclosure lets a reader judge quality, risks and limits, or only confirms that a thing exists.
pat.transparency-defined-down.fix: Specify the content of disclosures, including limits and known risks, and who receives them.
pat.transparency-defined-down.ex_ai: A bare statement that content is AI-generated is less informative than disclosing training data and limitations, and laws can require only the former.
pat.transparency-defined-down.ex_other: For illustration: a financial product bill could require a notice that fees apply without listing the amounts or when they are charged.
pat.labeling-reductionism.plain: Labeling is inexpensive and may have little effect on what people believe or do, but can be treated as sufficient in place of structural measures.
pat.labeling-reductionism.check: Find where a label, notice or watermark is the only duty. Ask what evidence shows it changes behavior and what happens when it is ignored, removed or unseen.
pat.labeling-reductionism.fix: Pair labels with substantive duties and test whether the labels work.
pat.labeling-reductionism.ex_ai: Labeling is inexpensive and may have little effect on belief, but can be treated as sufficient in place of structural measures.
pat.labeling-reductionism.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on sugary drinks might require only a warning label and no limit on marketing to children.
pat.access-to-proof.plain: The records needed to show a violation are held by the party being regulated, so without disclosure, subpoena or preservation powers, enforcers and injured people may be unable to prove a case.
pat.access-to-proof.check: Find who holds the evidence needed to prove a violation. Ask whether the text gives enforcers and private parties access, subpoena power and a duty to preserve records, or leaves proof to the regulated party.
pat.access-to-proof.fix: Add disclosure, subpoena and record preservation powers for enforcers and claimants.
pat.access-to-proof.ex_ai: Companies hold the data needed to prove harm, and without disclosure powers, subpoena authority or preservation duties, regulators and plaintiffs cannot get it.
pat.access-to-proof.ex_other: For illustration: A workplace safety law might rely on employer inspection logs while giving inspectors no power to compel them.
pat.evidentiary-trail.plain: Without a duty to keep records, a party can minimize what it logs, which makes later review and accountability difficult.
pat.evidentiary-trail.check: Find duties to keep logs or records. Ask whether a retention period, content and format are set, who can access them, and whether a party could avoid creating the records at all.
pat.evidentiary-trail.fix: Require creation and retention of defined records for a set period, with access for enforcers.
pat.evidentiary-trail.ex_ai: Without record retention duties, systems can minimize logging, which makes later accountability difficult.
pat.evidentiary-trail.ex_other: For illustration: A food safety rule might require tests but no storage of results, so past outbreaks cannot be traced.
pat.researcher-access.plain: Without statutory access rights, independent study of an industry depends on company goodwill, which can be withdrawn.
pat.researcher-access.check: Check whether outside researchers, auditors and journalists have a legal right to data or facilities. Ask who qualifies, who can refuse, and whether good-faith research is protected from legal threats.
pat.researcher-access.fix: Create a legal access right for vetted researchers, with safe harbor for good-faith work.
pat.researcher-access.ex_ai: Without statutory access rights, independent evaluation depends on company goodwill that can be withdrawn.
pat.researcher-access.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on hospital pricing could require posting prices but give researchers no right to the underlying billing data.
pat.whistleblower-absence.plain: Employees are a likely source of information about problems, and without legal protection they can be silenced or penalized for speaking.
pat.whistleblower-absence.check: Check whether the law protects people who report violations, including from retaliation, and whether it provides a safe channel. Ask who is covered, what remedy exists and who enforces it.
pat.whistleblower-absence.fix: Add anti-retaliation protection, confidential reporting channels and a remedy for retaliation.
pat.whistleblower-absence.ex_ai: Employees are a likely source of safety information, and without protection they can be silenced or penalized.
pat.whistleblower-absence.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on food plant safety might create inspection duties but offer no protection for workers who report violations.
pat.nda-enforceability.plain: If nondisclosure agreements stay fully enforceable, or exceptions apply only to confidential official channels, people may be unable to report concerns.
pat.nda-enforceability.check: Find how the law treats confidentiality agreements. Ask whether they can block reports to regulators or the public, and whether the exception covers more than one confidential channel.
pat.nda-enforceability.fix: Void agreement terms that bar lawful reporting and allow reports to regulators and others.
pat.nda-enforceability.ex_ai: If nondisclosure agreements stay fully enforceable, or exceptions apply only to confidential regulatory channels, employees may be unable to report safety concerns.
pat.nda-enforceability.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on nursing home care might protect reports to the state agency but leave non-disparagement clauses enforceable against talking to families.
pat.audit-scope.plain: Audits that are infrequent or narrow in scope can miss problems that develop between reviews or fall outside the items examined.
pat.audit-scope.check: Find audit or inspection duties. Ask how often they occur, what they cover, who performs them, and whether a fast changing product or practice could pass between audits.
pat.audit-scope.fix: Set review frequency by risk, include change triggered reviews and define full scope and auditor independence.
pat.audit-scope.ex_ai: Annual or narrowly scoped audits miss fast-changing systems and misuse.
pat.audit-scope.ex_other: For illustration: A building safety law might require one inspection every five years of listed items only, missing later repairs and unlisted hazards.
pat.training-data-provenance.plain: Without requirements to record where inputs came from, material of uncertain origin cannot be traced and its quality or legality stays unaccountable.
pat.training-data-provenance.check: Check whether the law requires records of the source of inputs, materials or data. Ask who keeps them, how long, and who can inspect them.
pat.training-data-provenance.fix: Require origin records for inputs, with retention periods and inspection rights.
pat.training-data-provenance.ex_ai: Without provenance requirements, training data of uncertain origin cannot be traced and inputs stay unaccountable.
pat.training-data-provenance.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on imported seafood could set quality rules but not require records of where the catch originated.
pat.retention-deletion-tension.plain: The tension between keeping records for accountability and deleting data for privacy can be invoked either way depending on convenience.
pat.retention-deletion-tension.check: Find duties to keep records and duties to delete data. Ask which prevails when they conflict, who decides, and whether a retention period is stated.
pat.retention-deletion-tension.fix: State which duty prevails in each case and set retention periods with exceptions for audits.
pat.retention-deletion-tension.ex_ai: The tension between keeping records for accountability and deleting data for privacy can be invoked either way depending on convenience.
pat.retention-deletion-tension.ex_other: For illustration: a bill requiring both audit logs and prompt deletion of customer data might let a firm cite either to avoid producing records.
pat.reported-vs-published.plain: Reports sent to regulators without public release prevent public pressure and comparison between firms.
pat.reported-vs-published.check: Find each reporting duty and who receives the report. Ask whether it is published, in what form, how soon, and who may keep it confidential.
pat.reported-vs-published.fix: Require public release of reports in summary or redacted form, with narrow confidentiality grounds.
pat.reported-vs-published.ex_ai: Reports sent to regulators without public release prevent public pressure and comparison.
pat.reported-vs-published.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on school safety incidents might require reports to a state office but exempt them from public records requests.
pat.aggregation-proof-reporting.plain: When each regulated party chooses its own reporting format or method, the resulting data cannot be compared, so patterns across the field stay hidden.
pat.aggregation-proof-reporting.check: Find reporting duties. Ask whether the text fixes a common template, metrics and method, or lets each reporter choose, and whether results could be compared across parties and years.
pat.aggregation-proof-reporting.fix: Require a standard template, defined metrics and a common method for all reporters.
pat.aggregation-proof-reporting.ex_ai: Reporting formats that differ between companies produce data that cannot be meaningfully compared.
pat.aggregation-proof-reporting.ex_other: For illustration: A school discipline reporting law might let each district define its own categories, so statewide totals cannot be compared.
pat.reporting-frequency-lag.plain: Annual reporting for things that change quickly means the information is always out of date by the time it is seen.
pat.reporting-frequency-lag.check: Find how often reports are due and how long after the period they are published. Ask how fast the subject changes and whether serious events must be reported sooner.
pat.reporting-frequency-lag.fix: Set report frequency to the pace of change and add prompt notice of serious events.
pat.reporting-frequency-lag.ex_ai: Annual reporting for systems that change weekly means information is always outdated.
pat.reporting-frequency-lag.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on wildfire risk equipment might require a yearly report though conditions change within days.
pat.severability-strategy.plain: A severability clause can keep less visible provisions alive when others fall, while omitting one can make challenges to the whole law riskier or safer.
pat.severability-strategy.check: Read the severability clause, or note its absence. Ask which provisions would survive if others were struck down, and whether the remainder still works as intended.
pat.severability-strategy.fix: Include a clear severability clause and consider which provisions are essential.
pat.hollow-savings-clause.plain: A clause preserving existing rights can be empty if the new framework makes those rights hard to use in practice.
pat.hollow-savings-clause.check: Read each clause saying the Act does not affect existing rights. Ask whether other provisions make those rights harder to use in practice, such as through procedure, forum or proof rules.
pat.hollow-savings-clause.fix: Back the savings clause with operative rules that keep the rights usable.
pat.common-law-preemption.plain: Silence on state common law claims, or a freeze on new state rules, can leave doubt over whether courts may develop liability theories.
pat.common-law-preemption.check: Search for language on state common law, tort claims or a bar on new state rules. Ask whether existing claims are preserved, and whether loose words such as 'requirements' could sweep them away.
pat.common-law-preemption.fix: State whether state tort and common law claims are preserved.
pat.common-law-preemption.ex_ai: AI bills can leave doubt over whether state tort claims survive, or can freeze state legal frameworks for AI.
pat.implied-repeal.plain: A later statute that is hard to reconcile with an earlier one leaves both on the books, creating uncertainty settled only by litigation.
pat.implied-repeal.check: Compare the new provisions with earlier laws on the same subject. Ask whether any conflict exists, and whether the text repeals or amends the earlier provision expressly instead of leaving courts to reconcile them.
pat.implied-repeal.fix: Repeal or amend the earlier provisions expressly.
pat.code-placement.plain: Where a provision is codified affects which agency runs it, which committees oversee it and which precedents apply.
pat.code-placement.check: Check where each provision is to be codified. Ask which agency, committee and body of precedent that location brings, and whether the placement matches the regime the bill describes.
pat.code-placement.fix: Choose placement with the intended regime and agency in mind and state it.
pat.section-230-interaction.plain: Whether a new activity counts as publishing or neutral hosting under an existing immunity can be unresolved, and the bill may be silent on it.
pat.section-230-interaction.check: Find any existing law that shields a class of actors from liability. Ask whether the bill says if it applies to the new activity, and who decides if the text is silent.
pat.section-230-interaction.fix: State whether the existing shield applies to the new conduct and, if so, with what limits.
pat.section-230-interaction.ex_ai: Whether algorithmic curation counts as publishing or neutral hosting is unresolved, and the bill may be silent on it.
pat.section-230-interaction.ex_other: For illustration: a bill creating duties for ride platforms might not say whether an older liability shield for intermediaries still applies.
pat.ip-laundering.plain: Treating AI outputs as original works can reduce the leverage of rights holders over the use of their work for training.
pat.ip-laundering.check: Find how the bill treats ownership of machine-generated output and the use of existing works as input. Ask whether the people whose works were used have any claim or notice.
pat.ip-laundering.fix: Address training use and output ownership expressly in the text.
pat.ip-laundering.ex_ai: Treating AI outputs as original works can reduce the leverage of rights holders over the use of their work for training.
pat.preempting-anti-discrimination.plain: A new, weaker standard on a topic can displace stronger claims under existing civil rights or consumer laws if the text is not clear about overlap.
pat.preempting-anti-discrimination.check: Find preemption, supremacy and savings language. Ask whether existing rights and remedies survive, and whether compliance with the new law is treated as compliance with older ones.
pat.preempting-anti-discrimination.fix: State that existing rights and remedies remain, and that compliance here does not excuse compliance elsewhere.
pat.preempting-anti-discrimination.ex_ai: Weaker AI-specific standards may displace stronger claims under existing civil rights laws.
pat.preempting-anti-discrimination.ex_ot: For illustration: a bill on tenant screening could set a mild fairness test and be read to replace stronger claims under housing law.
pat.ip-interactions.plain: Patents, copyright and trade secret protection can limit outside inspection and competition, which may block audits or reuse that the law otherwise expects.
pat.ip-interactions.check: Find disclosure and inspection duties. Ask whether trade secret or other intellectual property claims can block access, and whether confidential review by auditors or regulators is guaranteed.
pat.ip-interactions.fix: Provide confidential access for regulators and auditors that overrides trade secret objections.
pat.ip-interactions.ex_ai: Patents, copyrightable outputs and trade secret model weights together can limit auditing and competition.
pat.ip-interactions.ex_other: For illustration: A drug pricing law might require cost disclosure but let firms withhold figures as trade secrets.
pat.contract-supremacy.plain: Without a bar on waiver, standard form contracts can set aside protections the statute gives, so the protection depends on what a party signs.
pat.contract-supremacy.check: Find any rights or duties stated as defaults. Ask whether a contract, waiver or agreement can alter them, and whether the text says protections cannot be waived.
pat.contract-supremacy.fix: Add an anti-waiver clause and treat contrary terms as void.
pat.contract-supremacy.ex_ai: Without anti-waiver provisions, contracts of adhesion can set aside protections the statute gives.
pat.contract-supremacy.ex_other: For illustration: A tenant rights bill might not say lease terms cannot waive repair duties, so landlords can add a standard waiver.
pat.major-questions-trigger.plain: Grants of authority just ambiguous enough to be challenged under the major questions doctrine can face years of litigation.
pat.major-questions-trigger.check: Find grants of authority over matters of large economic or social reach. Ask whether the text states the power and its limits plainly, or relies on general words a court could find too thin.
pat.major-questions-trigger.fix: State the authority and its limits clearly, with specific findings on scope.
pat.chevron-vacuum.plain: With deference to agency readings gone, vague language is resolved by courts, which can delay or reverse agency interpretation.
pat.chevron-vacuum.check: Identify provisions that rely on the agency's reading of an unclear term. Ask whether a court, deciding the term for itself, could reach a different meaning, and whether the text states the agency's discretion expressly.
pat.chevron-vacuum.fix: Draft specifically or give express discretion to the agency.
pat.findings-for-deference.plain: Congressional findings shape how courts judge a law's constitutionality, and well-drafted or weakened findings change its vulnerability.
pat.findings-for-deference.check: Read the findings against the powers the bill uses. Ask whether they state specific facts tied to each power, and whether a court could use them or their absence to judge validity.
pat.findings-for-deference.fix: Include specific findings supported by record evidence.
pat.legislative-veto.plain: Legislative veto provisions are unenforceable but agencies often comply, creating congressional control through political norms.
pat.legislative-veto.check: Find provisions letting one chamber or a committee block or approve an agency action. Ask whether the action must pass through the ordinary lawmaking process, and what happens if the agency ignores the veto.
pat.legislative-veto.fix: Use joint resolutions subject to presentment instead of one-house vetoes.
pat.first-amendment-engineering.plain: A slightly overbroad provision can be struck on speech grounds, and the ruling can narrow what later laws are able to do.
pat.first-amendment-engineering.check: Find provisions that restrict or compel communication. Ask whether they are tailored to a stated interest, whether they are open to a speech challenge, and what a loss would mean for the rest of the law.
pat.first-amendment-engineering.fix: Tailor narrowly, state the interest, add severability and avoid needless content based triggers.
pat.first-amendment-engineering.ex_ai: Slightly overbroad provisions may be struck, and the resulting decision can narrow regulatory space for a generation.
pat.first-amendment-engineering.ex_other: For illustration: A disclosure law might compel detailed statements from any publisher, inviting a challenge that sets a broad precedent.
pat.takings-traps.plain: Provisions that compel sharing or access to property can draw takings challenges that could limit regulation of whole categories.
pat.takings-traps.check: Find any duty that forces a party to share, license or give access to assets. Ask whether compensation is addressed and whether a challenge could strike the broader scheme.
pat.takings-traps.fix: Provide compensation or narrow the compelled access, and include fallback provisions if challenged.
pat.takings-traps.ex_ai: Data sharing or forced access provisions can draw takings challenges that could limit regulation of whole categories.
pat.takings-traps.ex_other: For illustration: a bill forcing utilities to open private lines to competitors could be challenged for lack of compensation.
pat.due-process-hooks.plain: Strong procedures paired with vague standards can invite due process challenges that remove enforcement while the law remains on the books.
pat.due-process-hooks.check: Find enforcement powers and the standards they apply. Ask whether affected parties get fair notice, a hearing and a clear rule, or whether vagueness leaves the power open to challenge.
pat.due-process-hooks.fix: Pair strong powers with clear standards, notice, hearing and appeal rights.
pat.due-process-hooks.ex_ai: Aggressive procedures with vague standards invite due process challenges that can remove enforcement while leaving the law in place.
pat.due-process-hooks.ex_other: For illustration: A licensing law might allow immediate suspension for conduct harmful to the public, with no defined test or hearing.
pat.dormant-commerce-weaponization.plain: A provision that may conflict with limits on the enacting body's power can attract litigation, and the result or the threat of it can support arguments for a weaker uniform standard.
pat.dormant-commerce-weaponization.check: Find provisions that reach beyond the enacting body's territory or powers. Ask whether they are open to a structural legal challenge and what a loss would do to the rest of the law.
pat.dormant-commerce-weaponization.fix: Tie reach to local effects, add findings and severability, and avoid needless extraterritorial reach.
pat.dormant-commerce-weaponization.ex_ai: Vulnerable state laws can generate litigation that supports arguments for a weaker federal standard.
pat.dormant-commerce-weaponization.ex_ot: For illustration: A state labeling law might regulate out of state sales, drawing a challenge that ends in a weaker national standard.
pat.sense-of-congress.plain: A sense of Congress statement has no legal force but can be presented as if Congress took a position.
pat.sense-of-congress.check: Find statements of the legislature's sense or encouragement. Ask whether any operative duty follows, and whether the statement could be presented as a legal position.
pat.sense-of-congress.fix: Replace with an operative provision or remove it.
pat.aspirational-preamble.plain: A preamble declares bold goals while operative provisions contain qualifications that keep the goals from being achieved.
pat.aspirational-preamble.check: Set each goal in the purposes or findings beside the operative sections. Ask whether any qualifier, exemption or discretion in the operative text can keep that goal from being met, and whether purposes guide interpretation.
pat.aspirational-preamble.fix: Align operative text with each stated goal and state that purposes guide interpretation.
pat.innovation-defense.plain: Findings that regulation could leave a country behind can be cited later in rulemaking and cost-benefit analysis, shifting how the operative rules are read.
pat.innovation-defense.check: Find findings or purpose statements about competitiveness, growth or leadership. Ask whether they are tied to operative text and could be used to narrow duties or justify exemptions.
pat.innovation-defense.fix: Keep findings balanced and state that they do not limit protective duties.
pat.innovation-defense.ex_ai: Findings that regulation could cause the country to fall behind competitors can shape later rulemaking and cost-benefit analysis.
pat.innovation-defense.ex_other: For illustration: A telecom bill might include a finding that regulation threatens leadership, later cited to justify weaker rules.
pat.voluntary-commitments.plain: Voluntary pledges cited as proof that law is unnecessary can later be written into the law as its standard, fixing a low bar.
pat.voluntary-commitments.check: Find references to voluntary frameworks, pledges or best practices. Ask whether the law adopts them as its standard, who wrote them, and whether they are enforceable.
pat.voluntary-commitments.fix: Set the standard in the statute, with voluntary measures only as a floor.
pat.voluntary-commitments.ex_ai: Voluntary pledges cited as proof that law is unnecessary can later be written into the law as its standard.
pat.voluntary-commitments.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on data brokers might adopt an industry code of conduct as the legal safe harbor.
pat.tool-not-agent.plain: Describing a product as a mere tool, or by another label, can limit the responsibility of its maker and block rules suited to how it actually behaves.
pat.tool-not-agent.check: Find labels that describe what a thing is, such as tool, aid or assistant. Ask what legal consequences follow from the label, and whether the actual behavior fits.
pat.tool-not-agent.fix: Attach duties to function and effect rather than to a descriptive label.
pat.tool-not-agent.ex_ai: Describing AI as a tool can limit responsibility and block rules suited to autonomous systems.
pat.tool-not-agent.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on automated trading might call software a mere tool of the trader, so the maker faces no duty when it acts unexpectedly.
pat.bias-is-a-bug.plain: Describing a harm as a technical defect to be improved can make the remedy a fix by the operator, rather than a limit on where or whether the product is used.
pat.bias-is-a-bug.check: Find language that treats a harm as an error rate or defect. Ask whether the only remedy is improvement, and whether use can be limited, paused or prohibited if the defect persists.
pat.bias-is-a-bug.fix: Provide limits on use and remedies independent of whether the operator claims to have improved the product.
pat.bias-is-a-bug.ex_ai: Framing bias as a technical defect makes the remedy to improve the system and not to limit its use.
pat.bias-is-a-bug.ex_other: For illustration: A lending bill might require lenders to refine scoring methods after disparities appear, with no ability to restrict the method itself.
pat.humans-in-the-loop.plain: A requirement for human review can create the look of oversight when the reviewer lacks time, information or authority to depart from the recommended result.
pat.humans-in-the-loop.check: Find required human review or sign-off. Ask whether the reviewer has the time, training, information and power to disagree, and whether outcomes show how often they do.
pat.humans-in-the-loop.fix: Define meaningful review, give reviewers authority and time, and track override rates.
pat.humans-in-the-loop.ex_ai: A human review requirement can create the appearance of oversight when reviewers tend to accept the system's output.
pat.humans-in-the-loop.ex_other: For illustration: A loan rule might require an officer to sign each decision, though the officer has seconds per file and rarely overrules the score.
pat.assistance-without-assistance.plain: Support programs that are underfunded, mismatched to need or hard to qualify for can look like a response to harm while reaching few of the people affected.
pat.assistance-without-assistance.check: Find support or transition programs. Ask what funding, eligibility rules and application steps apply, how many people could realistically qualify, and whether the support matches the loss.
pat.assistance-without-assistance.fix: Fund assistance to match expected need and set simple eligibility and outcome reporting.
pat.assistance-without-assistance.ex_ai: Retraining or support programs that are underfunded, mismatched or hard to qualify for give the appearance of addressing displacement.
pat.assistance-without-assistance.ex_oth: For illustration: A plant closure law might offer retraining for jobs that do not exist locally, with enrollment limited to a small number of workers.
pat.impact-without-teeth.plain: Assessments that only inform, and do not affect whether or how something goes ahead, show people the harm while the project proceeds unchanged.
pat.impact-without-teeth.check: Find required assessments or statements. Ask whether any finding can delay, change or stop the activity, who can act on it, and whether the public can respond.
pat.impact-without-teeth.fix: Tie assessment findings to conditions, mitigation duties or review before the activity proceeds.
pat.impact-without-teeth.ex_ai: Informational assessments that do not affect deployment decisions show communities their harm while deployment goes ahead.
pat.impact-without-teeth.ex_other: For illustration: A development law might require a community impact report that expressly cannot hold up a building permit.
pat.adversary-argument.plain: Presenting each protective rule as helping a competitor or rival can make restraint look like a loss and can crowd out safeguards, even where the claim is untested.
pat.adversary-argument.check: Find statements that tie a safeguard to advantage for a rival nation, firm or sector. Ask what evidence supports the claim and whether the safeguard still operates independently of it.
pat.adversary-argument.fix: Require stated evidence for competitive claims and keep protective duties independent of them.
pat.adversary-argument.ex_ai: Framing every safety rule as helping a rival nation presents restraint as surrender and can crowd out safety measures.
pat.adversary-argument.ex_other: For illustration: A food import safety bill might be argued down on the ground that stricter inspection would hand business to foreign suppliers.
pat.incumbent-compliance-costs.plain: Heavy compliance requirements can act as barriers that large firms absorb and smaller or community competitors cannot, so a safeguard can also reduce competition.
pat.incumbent-compliance-costs.check: Find registration, licensing and compliance program duties. Ask what they cost, whether small actors can meet them, and whether duties scale with size and risk.
pat.incumbent-compliance-costs.fix: Scale duties to size and risk and provide support or simplified paths for small actors.
pat.incumbent-compliance-costs.ex_ai: Heavy compliance requirements can act as barriers that large firms can absorb and smaller or open source competitors cannot.
pat.incumbent-compliance-costs.ex_other: For illustration: A food safety bill might require a full time compliance officer, which a small producer cannot afford.
pat.data-moat.plain: Limits on gathering new resources can leave established firms with what they already hold while newcomers start with nothing, so a protective rule can also reduce competition.
pat.data-moat.check: Find rules that restrict collecting or acquiring an input. Ask whether existing holders keep their stock, whether entrants face the full restriction, and how the effect on competition was weighed.
pat.data-moat.fix: Apply restrictions to existing holdings in a comparable way or give entrants access to shared inputs.
pat.data-moat.ex_ai: Privacy rules limiting new collection can leave established firms with historic data while new entrants have none.
pat.data-moat.ex_other: For illustration: A licensing rule closing new permits for a resource might leave early permit holders with all of the supply.
pat.compute-thresholds.plain: A threshold set in a technical measure can stop tracking the real risk as technology changes, and can bind only the largest actors while leaving similar risks uncovered.
pat.compute-thresholds.check: Find every numeric threshold. Ask what it is measured in, whether that measure will still track the risk in five years, and whether an actor can stay just under it.
pat.compute-thresholds.fix: Pair thresholds with a risk based test and an update process, and add anti-evasion language.
pat.compute-thresholds.ex_ai: Thresholds set to capture only the largest labs impose costs that only well-resourced firms can handle and leave others unregulated.
pat.compute-thresholds.ex_other: For illustration: A chemical plant safety law might apply by storage volume of one substance, missing equally dangerous plants using a substitute.
pat.api-chokepoint.plain: Placing duties on whoever controls a single access point can make that party a gatekeeper and can shape or end other ways the product is distributed.
pat.api-chokepoint.check: Find the point in the supply or access chain where duties attach. Ask who controls it, what the duty gives them power to refuse, and what other distribution routes the rule affects.
pat.api-chokepoint.fix: State what the access point holder must and need not do, and protect lawful alternative routes.
pat.api-chokepoint.ex_ai: Rules at the API level make API controllers gatekeepers and can end open source distribution.
pat.api-chokepoint.ex_other: For illustration: A pharmacy law might place all dispensing duties on wholesalers, making them gatekeepers over which small pharmacies can stock a drug.
pat.procurement-standards.plain: Public purchasing rules can effectively set industry standards with little public scrutiny and can favor incumbents.
pat.procurement-standards.check: Find rules on government purchasing, contracts or acquisition that set requirements. Ask who writes them, whether the public can comment, and whether they favor firms already in the market.
pat.procurement-standards.fix: Open purchasing standards to public comment and set them to match the law's goals.
pat.procurement-standards.ex_ai: Federal procurement rules effectively set industry standards with little public scrutiny and can favor incumbents.
pat.procurement-standards.ex_other: For illustration: a bill on school technology could set purchasing requirements that only large vendors can meet.
pat.data-portability.plain: If moving data or accounts is hard or limited, switching costs remain high, so the law can appear to promote competition while changing little.
pat.data-portability.check: Find portability or transfer rights. Ask what format, scope and timing are required, whether the receiving party can use the result, and whether the right is enforceable in practice.
pat.data-portability.fix: Require standard formats, full scope, timely transfer and ongoing access for the receiving party.
pat.data-portability.ex_ai: Weak portability standards preserve switching costs while appearing pro-competitive.
pat.data-portability.ex_other: For illustration: A banking bill might let customers download statements as images, which cannot be loaded into another provider's system.
pat.interoperability.plain: Without interoperability, network effects can lock in leading providers, so whether to require it is a decision about market structure.
pat.interoperability.check: Find whether systems must work with others. Ask what standards, access and timing apply, and whether silence leaves leading providers able to keep users in.
pat.interoperability.fix: Require open, documented standards and access for competing providers.
pat.interoperability.ex_ai: Without interoperability, network effects lock in leading providers, so the choice is a market structure decision.
pat.interoperability.ex_other: For illustration: A payments bill might say nothing about connecting to other networks, leaving users tied to the largest one.
pat.vertical-integration.plain: Rules applying to one layer of a supply chain favor firms that span several layers and can shift costs between them.
pat.vertical-integration.check: Map the layers of the industry and see which the rules cover. Ask whether a firm operating in several layers can move costs or activity to an uncovered one.
pat.vertical-integration.fix: Apply rules to the integrated firm as a whole or add rules on dealings between its units.
pat.vertical-integration.ex_ai: Rules applying to one layer favor integrated firms that can shift costs between layers.
pat.vertical-integration.ex_other: For illustration: a bill capping fees by pharmacies might not cover a firm that owns both the insurer and the pharmacy.
pat.acquisition-thresholds.plain: Review triggers based on price or size can let most transactions pass unexamined, especially where the thing acquired has little or no sale price but large strategic value.
pat.acquisition-thresholds.check: Find the trigger for review of a transaction or entry. Ask what it is measured in, whether low priced or free items can fall below it, and whether data, users or capability could be counted instead.
pat.acquisition-thresholds.fix: Add review triggers based on factors such as users, data or capability, not price alone.
pat.acquisition-thresholds.ex_ai: High thresholds or price-based tests, often zero for free AI products, exempt most acquisitions.
pat.acquisition-thresholds.ex_other: For illustration: A hospital merger review law might trigger only above a dollar value, so purchases of small clinics with large local market share fall outside it.
pat.negative-pregnant.plain: Prohibiting one specific act can be read as allowing closely related conduct that the text does not mention.
pat.negative-pregnant.check: Find prohibitions that name one specific act. Ask whether closely related conduct is left outside, and whether a general prohibition or a statement that unlisted conduct is not authorized is present.
pat.negative-pregnant.fix: Add a general prohibition and state that unlisted related conduct is not authorized.
pat.tollgate-provision.plain: A permit or approval requirement with no deadline for the agency lets applications wait indefinitely, so approval may never arrive.
pat.tollgate-provision.check: Find each permit, license, approval or application step. Ask whether the agency has a decision deadline, and what happens to an applicant if it passes.
pat.tollgate-provision.fix: Set a decision deadline with automatic approval or a right to sue if it is missed.
pat.conference-rewrites.plain: Final text is reconciled by a small committee, so changes can occur with limited transparency after both chambers have debated.
pat.conference-rewrites.check: Compare the final text with the versions each chamber passed. Ask which provisions are new or changed, when the text was posted, and how long members had to read it before voting.
pat.conference-rewrites.fix: Require a waiting period and public posting of conference text before votes.
pat.signing-statements.plain: Presidential statements on how ambiguous provisions will be read signal how the law will be enforced without a vote.
pat.signing-statements.check: Compare the text with any statement by the signing official on how it will be read. Ask whether the statement narrows a provision, and whether the text settles the point itself.
pat.signing-statements.fix: Draft provisions specifically and track statements for effect.
pat.rider-omnibus-bundling.plain: Unrelated provisions placed in must-pass bills receive little scrutiny and can change unrelated policy areas.
pat.rider-omnibus-bundling.check: Look for provisions unrelated to the bill's main subject. Ask whether each has been separately debated, how much time readers had, and what unrelated policy it changes.
pat.rider-omnibus-bundling.fix: Require germane amendments and posting time for large bills.
pat.retroactive-redefinition.plain: A later law that clarifies an earlier one can reinterpret it in ways that conflict with original intent or settled court rulings.
pat.retroactive-redefinition.check: Find provisions described as clarifying earlier law. Ask whether they change what the earlier law was read to mean, and whether they apply to events or cases already underway.
pat.retroactive-redefinition.fix: Review later clarifying provisions against the original purpose and court readings.
pat.legislative-history-staging.plain: Floor statements and reports can be prepared to narrow or contradict plain text, and courts sometimes consult them.
pat.legislative-history-staging.check: Compare the text with reports and floor statements about it. Ask whether any statement narrows or contradicts the words, and whether the intended meaning is written into the bill itself.
pat.legislative-history-staging.fix: Write the intended meaning into the text itself.
pat.enrolled-bill-doctrine.plain: Once signed, the enrolled text is treated as conclusive even where it differs from what chambers voted on.
pat.enrolled-bill-doctrine.check: Compare the signed text with the text each chamber passed. Ask whether any word differs, and who is responsible for confirming they match before signature.
pat.enrolled-bill-doctrine.fix: Check enrolled text against passed text before signature.
pat.self-executing-rules.plain: A special rule can deem a bill passed without a separate vote, embedding policy that skips normal deliberation.
pat.self-executing-rules.check: Check whether a procedural rule deems the bill or text adopted. Ask whether members vote separately on the substance, and what policy sits inside the procedural measure.
pat.self-executing-rules.fix: Require separate recorded votes on substantive text.
pat.holman-rule.plain: Amendments to spending bills can cut named employees' pay to one dollar, neutralizing enforcement without touching the statute.
pat.holman-rule.check: Check appropriations text for limits on pay or positions of named people or offices. Ask whether the limit could stop a duty from being carried out while the statute stays unchanged.
pat.holman-rule.fix: Protect enforcement positions through statute and track appropriations amendments.
pat.technical-corrections.plain: Bills presented as fixing typos can make substantive changes that receive little scrutiny.
pat.technical-corrections.check: Read each section labeled technical or conforming. Ask whether any change alters who is covered, what is required or how much money is involved, beyond fixing errors.
pat.technical-corrections.fix: Limit technical corrections to enumerated typographic fixes with review.
pat.cra-window.plain: Rules finalized late in an administration can be repealed by the next Congress, and drafting affects how quickly rules can be finished.
pat.cra-window.check: Check the dates by which rules must be issued. Ask whether finalizing them near the end of an administration leaves them open to disapproval by the next legislature.
pat.cra-window.fix: Set deadlines that allow rules to be finalized outside the review window.
pat.committee-forum-shopping.plain: The committee a bill is sent to sets the expertise, priorities and interests that shape its text, so routing can influence the result.
pat.committee-forum-shopping.check: Identify which committee or body drafted or reviewed the bill. Ask whether its jurisdiction fits the subject, which other bodies had a claim, and how that routing could have shaped the wording.
pat.committee-forum-shopping.fix: Provide joint or sequential referral to bodies with relevant expertise.
pat.committee-forum-shopping.ex_ai: Committee assignment sets the lens through which a bill is written, so routing to one committee over another shapes the result.
pat.committee-forum-shopping.ex_other: For illustration: A bill on school food might go to a committee focused on agriculture, framing it around crop supply and not child nutrition.
pat.age-verification-poison-pill.plain: A required step that is costly, intrusive or hard to carry out can draw broad opposition and stall an otherwise supported bill, or be hard to comply with in practice.
pat.age-verification-poison-pill.check: Find any required verification, registration or documentation step. Ask whether it is feasible, what it costs users and regulated parties, and whether its burden could draw opposition that endangers the whole law.
pat.age-verification-poison-pill.fix: Use a feasible, privacy protective version of the step and keep it severable from the core duties.
pat.age-verification-poison-pill.ex_ai: Requiring age verification that is infeasible or invasive can generate opposition that sinks the whole bill.
pat.age-verification-poison-pill.ex_othe: For illustration: A tenant protection bill might require landlords to collect proof of income from every applicant, drawing objections that overshadow its main protections.
pat.strategic-complexity.plain: Text so long, layered or cross-referenced that few readers can find what it does can let a significant provision pass without scrutiny.
pat.strategic-complexity.check: Count the cross-references and nested exceptions a reader must follow to learn what one provision does. Ask whether the operative rule could be stated in one place.
pat.strategic-complexity.fix: State each operative rule in one place, limit nested cross-references, and supply a section-by-section summary that matches the text.
pat.strategic-complexity.ex_ai: Submitting thousands of pages of technical documentation can obscure information through volume.
pat.strategic-complexity.ex_other: For illustration: a benefits bill whose eligibility rule can only be found by reading four sections and two other statutes together.
pat.modifier-scope-after-a-list.plain: A qualifying phrase before or after a list can be read as applying to the nearest item or to every item.
pat.modifier-scope-after-a-list.check: Find each qualifying phrase placed before or after a list. Ask whether it applies to the nearest item or to every item, and whether a reasonable reader could pick either.
pat.modifier-scope-after-a-list.fix: Restructure the list into separate subparagraphs or repeat the modifier so its reach is explicit.
pat.and-and-or-in-conditions-and-negatio: A list of conditions joined by "and" or "or", especially under a negative, can be read as requiring all or any one.
Find lists of conditions joined by 'and' or 'or', especially under 'not' or 'no'. Ask whether the text requires all conditions or any one, and whether the reverse reading would change the result.
Use 'all of the following' or 'any of the following', and set conditions out as separate lettered items.
pat.punctuation-dependent-meaning.plain: The reach of a provision turns on a comma or its absence.
pat.punctuation-dependent-meaning.check: Find sentences where a comma or its absence changes who or what is covered. Ask what the sentence means with the punctuation removed, and whether another reading is plausible.
pat.punctuation-dependent-meaning.fix: Recast the sentence so its meaning does not depend on a comma, using separate clauses or subparagraphs.
pat.article-and-number-choice.plain: "A", "the" or a plural leaves open whether one item or several, or one document or several, satisfies the rule.
pat.article-and-number-choice.check: Find uses of 'a', 'the' or plural forms in duties and tests. Ask whether one item or several satisfies the rule, and whether one document, person or act is meant.
pat.article-and-number-choice.fix: State the number required, such as 'at least one' or 'each', instead of relying on articles or plurals.
pat.tense-that-leaves-earlier-conduct-in: A provision not written in the present tense leaves unclear whether it reaches conduct before enactment.
Find verbs in the past or future tense in operative provisions. Ask whether the provision reaches conduct before enactment, and whether the text says so.
Write operative provisions in the present tense and state expressly whether earlier conduct is covered.
pat.duty-with-no-named-actor.plain: A passive sentence states that something "shall be done" without saying who must do it.
pat.duty-with-no-named-actor.check: Find passive sentences saying something 'shall be done'. For each, ask who must do it, and who answers if it is not done.
pat.duty-with-no-named-actor.fix: Name the responsible official or body in each duty, and state the consequence of not acting.
pat.shall-used-to-state-a-rule-or-status: "Shall" appears where no one has a duty, blurring commands with declarations.
Find uses of 'shall' where no person has a duty, such as statements of status or effect. Ask whether a command or a declaration is meant.
Use 'is' or 'has' for statements of status and reserve 'shall' for duties with a named actor.
pat.prohibition-silent-on-acts-done-in-v: A "shall not" or "may not" does not say whether an act done in violation is void.
Find each 'shall not' or 'may not' and ask whether an act done in violation is void, voidable or valid. Ask who can challenge it.
State the legal effect of an act done in violation, such as that it is void or voidable, and who may raise it.
pat.proviso-of-uncertain-reach.plain: "Provided that" language leaves unclear whether it is a condition, an exception or a new rule, and what it attaches to.
pat.proviso-of-uncertain-reach.check: Find each 'provided that' clause. Ask whether it sets a condition, an exception or a new rule, and which words it attaches to.
pat.proviso-of-uncertain-reach.fix: Replace the proviso with a separate sentence or subsection stating whether it is a condition, an exception or a rule.
pat.varying-words-for-one-thing.plain: Different words for the same idea, or one word in two senses, invite a court to presume different meanings.
pat.varying-words-for-one-thing.check: Compare the words used for the same idea across sections. Ask whether a court could presume different meanings, and whether one word is used in two senses.
pat.varying-words-for-one-thing.fix: Use one term for one idea throughout and define it once.
pat.surplus-words.plain: Redundant words or doublets let a party argue that a broad reading makes another clause meaningless.
pat.surplus-words.check: Find doublets and repeated phrases such as 'rules and regulations'. Ask whether a party could argue a broad reading makes another clause meaningless, or that each word must add something.
pat.surplus-words.fix: Delete redundant words, or state that paired terms are to be read together.
pat.time-computation-gaps.plain: "Within", "before" and "after" leave a start point or the named date itself uncovered.
pat.time-computation-gaps.check: Find each 'within', 'before' and 'after' period. Ask when the clock starts, whether the named date itself is included, and who decides if the start is unclear.
pat.time-computation-gaps.fix: State the start event, the end date and whether both are included, and how weekends and holidays are treated.
pat.condition-placed-in-one-subpart.plai: Text inside one subparagraph, or flush text after a list, leaves unclear which sibling provisions it governs.
pat.condition-placed-in-one-subpart.chec: Find text inside one subparagraph or flush text after a list. Ask which sibling provisions it governs, and whether the layout answers that.
pat.condition-placed-in-one-subpart.fix: Move the condition into its own provision or repeat it in each subpart it governs.
pat.deem-used-for-a-judgment.plain: "Deems" is used for an exercise of judgment instead of a legal fiction, leaving the standard unclear.
pat.deem-used-for-a-judgment.check: Find each use of 'deem' or 'deemed'. Ask whether a legal fiction is meant or an exercise of judgment, and what standard guides the decision.
pat.deem-used-for-a-judgment.fix: Use 'deemed' only for legal fictions and state the standard where an official must judge.
pat.drafting-slip-with-substantive-effec: A wrong cross-reference, omitted item or typographical error changes the result.
Check cross-references, lists and numbers for wrong citations, omitted items and typographical errors. Ask whether correcting each would change who is covered or what is required.
Verify every cross-reference and list against the text before enactment, and add a correction process for later errors.
pat.inconsistent-base-in-parallel-clause: Two parallel provisions compute on different bases, such as gross against net.
Compare parallel provisions that compute amounts, such as gross against net. Ask whether the same base is used in each and whether the difference changes the result.
Define the base once and use it in each parallel clause.
pat.unreconciled-drafts-within-one-act.p: A phrase in one section does not fit the structure of the rest of a long act assembled from separate drafts.
pat.unreconciled-drafts-within-one-act.c: Read the long act for phrases that do not fit its overall structure or defined terms. Ask whether sections were drafted separately and whether they still agree.
pat.unreconciled-drafts-within-one-act.f: Run a conformity review of terms, definitions and structure across the whole text before enactment.
pat.title-or-heading-at-odds-with-the-te: A short title, heading or slogan describes more or less than the operative words do.
Compare each title, heading or slogan with the operative words beneath it. Ask whether it describes more or less than the text does.
Make headings accurate descriptions, and state that headings do not affect meaning.
pat.bill-text-length-that-hides-the-rule: Excess length and nesting obscure the operative rule.
Find the operative rule in the longest or most nested sections. Ask whether a reader can state it in one sentence, and how many cross-references are needed.
Move the core rule to a short, early provision and reduce nesting.
pat.canons-available-on-both-sides.plain: An ambiguous sentence can be argued under opposing canons, so the outcome cannot be predicted from the text.
pat.canons-available-on-both-sides.check: Find ambiguous sentences and ask which interpretive canons each side could cite. Ask whether the outcome could be predicted from the text alone.
pat.canons-available-on-both-sides.fix: Resolve the ambiguity in the text and add a construction rule stating the intended breadth.
pat.means-where-an-open-list-was-intende: A definition uses "means", which is exhaustive, although the drafter intended examples.
Find definitions beginning 'means' and ask whether the list is meant to be exhaustive. Ask whether examples were intended and later items could be left out.
Use 'includes' for examples and reserve 'means' for exhaustive definitions.
pat.operative-rule-inside-a-definition.p: A duty, exception or condition is placed in a definition where readers and codifiers do not expect it.
pat.operative-rule-inside-a-definition.c: Read definitions for duties, exceptions or conditions. Ask whether a reader looking at the operative sections would find them there.
pat.operative-rule-inside-a-definition.f: Move operative content into the operative sections and keep definitions to meaning only.
pat.context-escape-wording-in-a-definiti: "Unless the context requires otherwise" lets the defined meaning be set aside case by case.
Find 'unless the context requires otherwise' in a definition. Ask who decides when the context differs, and where the defined meaning could be set aside.
Delete the clause or list the specific contexts where a different meaning applies.
pat.defined-term-far-from-ordinary-meani: A label is given a meaning that departs from common usage, or is too bland to signal its content.
Compare each defined term with its everyday meaning. Ask whether the label misleads, or is too bland to signal what it covers.
Use a label that reflects the content of the definition, or avoid reusing an ordinary word with a special meaning.
The bill silently relies on, or collides with, Title 1 defaults such as "person" including corporations.
Find terms such as 'person' that are not defined in the bill. Ask whether general default definitions apply, and whether they fit the bill's purpose.
Define key terms in the bill instead of relying on general defaults, or state which default applies.
pat.status-label-without-a-functional-te: Treatment turns on a label such as "limited partner" or "corporation" that a party can adopt without changing what it does.
Find rules that turn on a status label. Ask whether a party could adopt the label without changing what it does, and whether a functional test is present.
Add a functional test describing what the party does, alongside or in place of the label.
Workers managed by algorithms may not be legally recognized as employees, leaving employment protections outside reach.
pat.definition-bound-to-older-technology: An element or definition describes the technology of its day and does not fit what replaced it.
Find definitions that describe a specific method, device or medium. Ask whether a replacement technology would fall outside, and who can update the definition.
Define by function rather than by method, and give a body authority to update the definition.
pat.definition-that-sweeps-in-bystanders: A definition is broad enough to reach people or everyday conduct outside the stated aim, with limits left to official assurance or prosecutorial choice.
Test each broad definition against everyday conduct outside the bill's aim. Ask whether limits rest on official assurance rather than text.
Add express exclusions and a purpose or intent element so the definition reaches only the intended conduct.
pat.general-term-beyond-expected-applica: A broad word reaches cases the enacting legislature did not picture.
Find broad words and ask what cases the drafters did not picture. Ask whether the outcome in those cases fits the purpose.
State the purpose in the text and add a rule on how courts should treat cases outside the expected applications.
pat.two-scopes-within-one-bill.plain: Different sections of the same bill define the covered class differently.
pat.two-scopes-within-one-bill.check: Compare how each section describes the covered class. Ask whether they differ, and which one governs where they conflict.
pat.two-scopes-within-one-bill.fix: Define the covered class once and use that term in every section.
pat.terms-inconsistent-with-the-amended-: Inserted text uses words that mean something different in the statute it amends or in a neighboring one.
Compare inserted words with the same words in the statute being amended and neighboring statutes. Ask whether they carry different meanings there.
Conform inserted terms to the amended statute, or define them for the inserted text.
pat.omitted-case.plain: The text is silent on a category or situation, and courts treat the silence as deliberate.
pat.omitted-case.check: List the categories and situations a reader would expect the text to address. Ask which are missing and whether a court could treat the silence as deliberate.
pat.omitted-case.fix: Add a catch-all or a statement of how omitted cases are treated, and name the cases that are meant to be left out.
pat.bright-line-that-invites-design-arou: A rule is so specific that conduct just outside it escapes.
Find precise thresholds and cutoffs. Ask what conduct just outside them would escape, and whether the purpose is served by that result.
Pair the bright line with an anti-avoidance rule and a power to adjust it by rule.
pat.self-determined-coverage.plain: The regulated party decides whether it is covered, with no registry or record of the decision.
pat.self-determined-coverage.check: Find tests the regulated party applies to itself. Ask whether any registry, notice or record shows who decided it is covered or not, and who can check.
pat.self-determined-coverage.fix: Require registration or a written determination that the agency can inspect, and let the agency make its own coverage finding.
pat.no-anti-evasion-clause.plain: Nothing reaches conduct that is restructured, relabeled or routed through another person to fall outside the mandate.
pat.no-anti-evasion-clause.check: Look for any rule reaching conduct that is restructured, relabeled or routed through another person. Ask what stops a party from arranging around the mandate.
pat.no-anti-evasion-clause.fix: Add an anti-avoidance clause covering arrangements whose main purpose is to avoid the rule.
pat.no-substance-over-form-backstop.plai: Compliance is judged by form alone, so arrangements with no purpose beyond avoiding the rule still qualify.
pat.no-substance-over-form-backstop.chec: Find compliance tests judged by form alone. Ask whether an arrangement with no purpose beyond avoiding the rule could still qualify.
pat.no-substance-over-form-backstop.fix: Add a rule that arrangements without a purpose other than avoidance are disregarded.
pat.thresholds-without-aggregation.plain: A size, volume or notification threshold applies entity by entity or transaction by transaction, so splitting avoids it.
pat.thresholds-without-aggregation.check: Find size, volume or notice thresholds that apply entity by entity or transaction by transaction. Ask whether splitting activity would avoid them.
pat.thresholds-without-aggregation.fix: Add aggregation rules treating related entities and linked transactions as one.
pat.thresholds-without-aggregation.ex_ai: A minimum size below which a deployment is ignored can exempt many small deployments that together have large effects.
pat.blending-to-qualify.plain: Favored activity or property can be added so that a mixed whole meets a test.
pat.blending-to-qualify.check: Find tests applied to a mixed whole, such as a share or ratio. Ask whether favored items could be added to meet the test, and how the mix is measured and checked.
pat.blending-to-qualify.fix: Measure the test on the underlying components and add a rule against adding items mainly to meet it.
pat.uncovered-close-substitute.plain: A rule names one item, asset type or instrument and a near-equivalent is left outside it.
pat.uncovered-close-substitute.check: Find rules naming one item, asset or instrument. Ask what close equivalent is left outside, and whether the purpose would be served by covering it.
pat.uncovered-close-substitute.fix: Define the covered category by function and include close substitutes, with a power to extend it by rule.
pat.recharacterization-into-a-favored-ca: Income, activity or a worker's status can be relabeled to enter a category with lighter treatment.
Find categories with lighter treatment. Ask whether income, activity or status could be relabeled to enter them, and who checks the label.
Add a substance based test for the favored category and a rule that disregards relabeling without a change in substance.
pat.unequal-treatment-of-close-equivalen: Two near-identical activities are treated very differently, so shifting between them pays.
Compare treatment of near identical activities. Ask whether the difference is large enough that parties would shift between them, and whether the purpose justifies it.
Align the treatment of close equivalents, or add a rule limiting the benefit of shifting.
pat.round-trip-transactions.plain: A transaction can be routed out and back to pick up a benefit.
pat.round-trip-transactions.check: Look for benefits tied to a location, party or category. Ask whether a transaction could go out and back to pick up the benefit.
pat.round-trip-transactions.fix: Add a rule denying the benefit to transactions that return to the original party or place, and require reporting.
pat.related-party-attribution-gap.plain: Family members, trusts or affiliates are not attributed to the covered person, so limits can be multiplied or sidestepped.
pat.related-party-attribution-gap.check: Find limits that apply to one person. Ask whether family members, trusts or affiliates are attributed to that person, and whether limits could be multiplied.
pat.related-party-attribution-gap.fix: Add attribution rules that treat related persons and controlled entities as one for each limit.
pat.duty-on-one-link-in-a-chain.plain: An obligation binds one actor while affiliates, intermediaries or controlling persons remain free to do the same thing.
pat.duty-on-one-link-in-a-chain.check: Identify the one actor the duty binds. Ask whether affiliates, intermediaries or controlling persons could do the same thing outside the duty.
pat.duty-on-one-link-in-a-chain.fix: Extend the duty to controlling persons and intermediaries, or add a rule making them answerable for evasion.
pat.election-into-a-lighter-parallel-reg: A party can register or qualify under a second statute with lighter duties.
Find other statutes under which a party could register or qualify with lighter duties. Ask whether this bill addresses that choice.
State which regime governs when more than one applies, and bar election into the lighter one for the same activity.
pat.timing-moves-around-a-date.plain: Parties shift transactions across an effective date or holding period.
pat.timing-moves-around-a-date.check: Find effective dates and holding periods. Ask whether transactions could be moved across them, and whether a look back or anti-timing rule exists.
pat.timing-moves-around-a-date.fix: Add a look back period and a rule disregarding transactions timed mainly to fall on the favorable side of a date.
pat.netting-that-cancels-a-charge.plain: Offset rules let a new tax or duty be reduced toward zero.
pat.netting-that-cancels-a-charge.check: Find offset, credit and netting rules attached to a new charge or duty. Ask whether they could reduce it toward zero.
pat.netting-that-cancels-a-charge.fix: Cap offsets, or provide a minimum amount that cannot be netted away.
pat.offsetting-response-by-another-gover: A state or other government can redesign its own law to neutralize the federal limit.
Find limits placed on another level of government. Ask whether it could redesign its own law to neutralize the limit, and whether the text anticipates that.
Add a rule addressing offsetting changes by other governments, and a reporting duty to track them.
pat.single-enforcer.plain: Only one federal agency may enforce, with no parallel authority for state attorneys general.
pat.single-enforcer.check: Find who may enforce. Ask whether state officials or others have parallel authority, and what happens if the one enforcer does not act.
pat.single-enforcer.fix: Give parallel enforcement authority to state officials and allow a private right of action as a backstop.
pat.no-reward-for-insiders.plain: The bill at most protects whistleblowers and offers no relator suit or bounty.
pat.no-reward-for-insiders.check: Look for protection, rewards or suit rights for insiders who report violations. Ask whether reporting carries any benefit beyond protection from retaliation.
pat.no-reward-for-insiders.fix: Add an insider reporting right with a share of recoveries, and protection from retaliation.
pat.private-right-without-economics.plai: A right to sue exists without statutory or multiplied damages or fee shifting, so small claims are not worth bringing.
pat.private-right-without-economics.chec: Find any right to sue and read the remedies. Ask whether damages, multiples or fee shifting make a small claim worth bringing.
pat.private-right-without-economics.fix: Add statutory or multiplied damages and shifting of reasonable fees to a prevailing plaintiff.
pat.fees-lost-on-voluntary-compliance.pl: Fee shifting applies only to judgments, so a defendant can comply after suit and avoid fees.
pat.fees-lost-on-voluntary-compliance.ch: Read the fee shifting terms. Ask whether fees are available only after a judgment, and whether a defendant could comply after suit and avoid them.
pat.fees-lost-on-voluntary-compliance.fi: Allow fees where the suit prompted the change in conduct, not only after judgment.
pat.non-enforcement-left-unreviewable.pl: No standards or triggers say when the agency must enforce, so a decision not to enforce, including for a whole category, cannot be challenged.
pat.non-enforcement-left-unreviewable.ch: Find standards for when the agency must enforce. Ask whether a decision not to enforce, including for a whole category, can be challenged.
pat.non-enforcement-left-unreviewable.fi: State criteria or triggers for enforcement and allow review of a refusal to enforce, with a reporting duty.
pat.statutory-damages-without-concrete-h: Fixed damages for a bare violation leave many plaintiffs without standing in federal court.
Find fixed damages for a bare violation. Ask whether a plaintiff must show concrete harm to sue in federal court, and which plaintiffs would be left out.
Define the injury the provision addresses, allow other enforcers to sue, and provide an alternative forum.
pat.agency-penalties-without-a-court-pat: Civil penalties can be imposed only in the agency's own tribunal, which is open to a jury-trial challenge.
Find civil penalties imposed in the agency's own tribunal. Ask whether a court route exists, and whether a jury trial challenge could stall them.
Provide a court action for penalties as an alternative to the agency tribunal.
pat.funding-conditions-without-rights-la: Duties are written as conditions on grants without clear rights-creating terms, so beneficiaries cannot sue.
Find duties written as conditions on grants. Ask whether the text uses clear rights creating language, and whether beneficiaries could sue.
Use express rights creating language and state who may enforce it.
pat.independence-resting-on-removal-prot: The design assumes enforcers cannot be removed at will.
Find protections that assume enforcers cannot be removed at will. Ask what happens to the design if a court finds those protections invalid.
Add a fallback structure that keeps the body's function if removal protection is invalidated.
pat.missing-clear-statement-on-states.pl: The bill alters the federal-state balance or subjects states to suit without the explicit statement courts require.
pat.missing-clear-statement-on-states.ch: Find provisions that change the federal and state balance or subject states to suit. Ask whether the text says so explicitly in the way courts require.
pat.missing-clear-statement-on-states.fi: State the intended effect on state governments in clear express terms.
pat.mental-state-unstated-or-set-high.pl: A penalty provision is silent on mental state, or liability attaches only to "willful" or "knowing" violations.
pat.mental-state-unstated-or-set-high.ch: Find penalty provisions and read the mental state required. Ask whether it is unstated, or limited to 'willful' or 'knowing' acts, and what a regulated party could claim not to know.
pat.mental-state-unstated-or-set-high.fi: State the required mental state and provide for civil liability without proof of intent.
pat.ambiguity-in-a-penalty-provision.pla: Unclear words in a provision carrying criminal penalties are read for the defendant, and that reading can carry into civil cases.
pat.ambiguity-in-a-penalty-provision.che: Find unclear words in provisions carrying criminal penalties. Ask whether the narrower reading would be applied, and whether that reading could carry into civil cases.
pat.ambiguity-in-a-penalty-provision.fix: Define the key terms of any penalty provision and separate the civil standard from the criminal one.
pat.narrowing-by-constitutional-doubt.pl: A party can win a narrow reading by raising a serious constitutional question without winning the constitutional claim.
pat.narrowing-by-constitutional-doubt.ch: Find provisions that could raise a serious constitutional question. Ask whether a court could adopt a narrow reading to avoid it.
pat.narrowing-by-constitutional-doubt.fi: Include a clear statement of intended breadth and findings supporting the provision.
pat.gates-on-private-suits.plain: A mandatory notice period, a bar when the government is "diligently prosecuting", or a government power to dismiss lets a suit be headed off.
pat.gates-on-private-suits.check: Find notice periods, bars during government prosecution and government powers to dismiss. Ask whether a suit could be headed off by them.
pat.gates-on-private-suits.fix: Limit the notice period, define when a government action blocks a suit, and require court approval of dismissals.
pat.private-relator-open-to-challenge.pl: Enforcement by relators on the government's behalf faces unresolved Article II objections.
pat.private-relator-open-to-challenge.ch: Find enforcement by private parties on the government's behalf. Ask what constitutional objections could be raised and what happens if they succeed.
pat.private-relator-open-to-challenge.fi: Add a government enforcement path that continues if the relator mechanism is invalidated.
pat.past-violations-not-actionable.plain: Private suits reach only ongoing or future violations, or only forward-looking relief.
pat.past-violations-not-actionable.check: Read what private suits may reach. Ask whether past violations can be sued over or only ongoing ones, and whether only forward looking relief is available.
pat.past-violations-not-actionable.fix: Allow suit over past violations within a stated period and provide for damages as well as forward looking relief.
pat.limitation-period-that-never-restart: The period runs from the first act and does not restart with each continuing effect.
Find limitation periods and their start points. Ask whether each continuing effect restarts the clock or only the first act counts.
State that each continuing violation or new effect starts a new period.
pat.no-time-limit-on-rule-challenges.pla: The bill relies on the general six-year limit, which restarts for each newly injured party.
pat.no-time-limit-on-rule-challenges.che: Look for a time limit on challenges to rules made under the bill. Ask whether the general default period applies and when it restarts.
pat.no-time-limit-on-rule-challenges.fix: State a specific filing period for challenges and when it starts.
pat.filing-rule-readable-as-jurisdiction: A deadline or precondition is worded so that a court treats it as a limit on its power, not a waivable rule.
Find deadlines and preconditions to suit. Ask whether the wording could be read as a limit on the court's power instead of a waivable rule.
Word deadlines as claim processing rules and state that they may be waived or tolled.
pat.private-trigger-open-to-misuse.plain: A private notice or complaint compels action with no penalty for false notices, no counter-notice and too little time to verify.
pat.private-trigger-open-to-misuse.check: Find private notices or complaints that compel action. Ask what penalizes false ones, whether a counter notice exists, and whether time to verify is enough.
pat.private-trigger-open-to-misuse.fix: Add a penalty for false notices, a counter notice process and a reasonable verification period.
